title: Downloaded mail paging and counts
blurb: Previous and Next show up to 200 downloaded messages per page. A read message held open in Unread appears only on its ordered page. Per-account Starred and Unread refresh when downloaded mail changes in that account’s folders. Unfiltered chronological pages use a validated forward cursor and bounded per-mailbox merges. Previous reuses up to 32 saved boundaries; ordinary refreshes retain the current boundary only if the host validates its scope, ordering and snooze version. Older boundaries, filtered views and stale versions fall back to offset paging. Scope changes clear saved boundaries. Exact downloaded totals and oldest dates remain separate from provider folder counts. Badge reads skip oldest-date aggregation; unrelated accounts, cosmetic changes and sync progress keep cached counts. Unread summaries cache the ordinary unread aggregate independently of the selected held read row, then validate that row against scope, exclusions and snoozes. Unread and Starred pages use partial indexes. Gmail seeds exact local folder counts once on first use, then commits insert, unread, move and deletion deltas with each content/resume acknowledgement; cursor-only saves reuse them. IMAP reuses supplied counts and checks 64 visited identity/flag rows per reconciliation page against one UID set, yielding even when nothing is deleted. Incomplete UID searches cannot imply deletion. Search ranking, sparse filters, offset fallback and individual disk calls can still pause work.
